# Lossless configuration upgrades

Convert shared-context-routes/v2 to shared-context-routes/v3, or shared-context-layout/v1 to shared-context-layout/v2. Validate the exact source first. Replace only the top-level numeric schema assignment with the declared schemaVersion assignment. Preserve comments, unknown route metadata, ordering, whitespace outside that assignment, and all configured values. Reject alternate header syntax that cannot be replaced without a decision. Validate the destination and compare parsed meaning plus normalized authored text before persistence.

Only the installed scripts/shared-context/contracts.ts adapter executes this procedure. The shared skill-contracts writer owns locking, file identity checks, atomic replacement, and bulk partial outcomes. Event and artifact paths are immutable. Read-only commands never invoke conversion. Configuration content upgrade does not authorize storage migration.

# Explicit grooming upgrades

Resolve this installed skill as `GROOMING_SKILL_ROOT`. Run its absolute scripts from the target repository.

```sh
"$GROOMING_SKILL_ROOT/scripts/grooming-report.ts" upgrade /absolute/selected-paths.json
```

The input is a JSON array of distinct artifact paths. The command uses shared `bulkUpgrade` with `scripts/report-owner.ts`. Each source must validate. Each destination must validate and preserve all authored content before shared atomic persistence. Partial results return nonzero and retain each item outcome. No upgrade command applies tracker actions.

Declared edges are `grooming-report/v1` to `grooming-report/v2`, and `grooming-actions/v1` to `grooming-actions/v2`. Reports gain an explicit identifier. Their YAML comments, unknown metadata, body, evidence, verdicts and actions remain byte-for-byte unchanged except the identifier line. Noncanonical explicit identifier syntax is refused instead of rewriting YAML. Actions gain the v2 envelope; all original ticket records and unknown fields remain intact. Ambiguous or non-round-tripping JSON content is refused.

Read-only `check`, `render` input reading, and `check-actions` use historical readers, not upgrades. Published history under `artifacts`, `events`, `receipts`, `evidence`, or `snapshots` is immutable and requires these readers. Symlinks and hard links are rejected by the shared writer. Unknown identifiers, invalid source or destination content, loss, and decision-dependent conversions preserve source bytes and return nonzero. Already-current valid artifacts remain byte-identical.

## Inventory

| Boundary | Direction | Definition and validator | Compatibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Research report | Both | report-contract.md; parseReport | v1 historical reader; v2 output; declared safe upgrade |
| Proposed action record | Both | contracts/actions-v2.md; readActions | bare-array v1 reader; v2 envelope output; declared safe upgrade |
| contracts.json | Input | skill-contracts built-in manifest | shared loadContracts |
| HTML report and prose summary | Output | HTML and human-readable prose | no internal machine contract |
| tickets.txt | Input | newline-separated opaque ticket selectors | no injected identifier |
| selected-paths.json | Input | shared bulkUpgrade path list | shared API validation |
| applied.json | Output | user-selected ticket-operation audit, not compilation input | ticket skill owns mutation results; never inferred from proposed actions |

## Change log

- Added current report identities and action envelopes. Kept read-only historical readers. Added explicit shared safe upgrades and checked action consumption.

# Mutable view upgrade

This procedure applies only to generated `manifest.yaml` and `projections/latest-status.yaml` in the resolved workflow. It is not authority to mutate a workflow.

1. Validate the exact source contract and path with `scripts/view-contracts.ts`. Bind `manifest.yaml` to the `worktree-workflow` family and `projections/latest-status.yaml` to `worktree-latest-status`, for both current and historical versions. Swapped families fail before conversion or mutation, including public bulk upgrades.
2. For `worktree-workflow/v2` to `worktree-workflow/v3`, rename the scalar key `schema` to `schemaVersion` and change its value. For `worktree-latest-status/v1` to `worktree-latest-status/v2`, apply the same field change.
3. Preserve every other YAML node, unknown property, comment and authored value. Compare canonical YAML after normalizing only the contract key/value. Reject aliases, explicit tags and numeric values that cannot be represented safely.
4. Validate the destination and the requested generated-field update before replacing bytes through the shared safe-upgrade operation. All writers must honor its sibling lock.

No unversioned detector is declared. Unknown or conflicting identifiers fail. Events, receipts, reviews, snapshots and hash-linked history are immutable and have no upgrade path. Read them through their explicit historical readers. Rejected requests leave source bytes unchanged.

## Initiative boundary

Current manifests require `initiative: null` or a nonempty initiative ID containing letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens. Historical v2 validation retains its original semantics. Conversion requires an explicit valid initiative. Missing or invalid historical membership needs an owner decision; the converter never invents membership or writes a supposedly lossless upgrade.

type: Procedure

# Tracker record upgrades

The installed scripts/record-upgrade.ts adapter implements these declared edges. Each ticket source converts only to tracker-ticket/v2. Each initiative source converts only to tracker-initiative/v2. Supported sources are the exact historical v1 and explicit unversioned legacy contracts.

Validate the source before conversion. Remove only the plain identifier line. Preserve its inline comment as a standalone comment. Insert schemaVersion with the destination identifier. Preserve every other byte, including specification text, comments, unknown YAML, numeric spelling, identity, membership links and direct blockers. Compare the raw content with only the identifier removed before persistence. Compare initiative membership under each source and destination reader too. Reject unversioned initiatives whose body links would change membership when only the Tickets section becomes authoritative. Reject unsupported spellings or content that cannot meet this check.

Only mutable Markdown records can convert. Reject immutable records and paths under events, reviews, artifacts or .git. The record identity must match its ticket filename or initiative directory. Historical plans and event chains have readers, not upgrade edges.

The shared safeUpgrade and bulkUpgrade APIs own declaration validation, path selection, locks, byte checks and atomic persistence. Installation and read-only commands never invoke this adapter. Authorize update before calling safeUpgrade. The update request accepts only non-empty title, work_status and triage strings under fields. Structural changes require their existing tracker operation. The destination validator runs after mutation.

Explicit bulk conversion reports each persisted outcome. A rejected item keeps its original bytes. Earlier successful items remain converted when another item fails. A current valid record remains byte-identical.



Ticket update and bulk upgrade preflight the direct parent initiative before persistence. Follow ticket parents for supported hierarchical membership. Validate the complete initiative Tickets index against all direct children. Reject inconsistent membership without changing the selected ticket. Standalone tickets remain supported. Bulk items with unrelated valid membership remain independent.

# Setup contract upgrade procedure

## Declared edges

- `tracker-setup-answers/v1` to `tracker-setup-answers/v2`.
- `tracker-setup-state/v1` to `tracker-setup-state/v2`.

The procedure reference is `file:references/setup-contracts/upgrade-v1-v2.md`. The installed owner adapter is the default export of `file:scripts/setup.ts`. The shared `skill-contracts` engine selects declared paths, validates both contracts, compares preservation values, and owns atomic single-artifact persistence. No numeric version ordering selects a path.

## Source validation

Historical answers and state use numeric `schema: 1` with no `schemaVersion`. Current answers and state use their exact v2 `schemaVersion` and forbid `schema`. Identify the historical record kind from its validated content: state has a managed `files` array; answers have tracker decisions. Reject mixed or unknown explicit identities, unsupported operations, missing required fields, unknown answer keys, unknown state keys, unknown managed-file keys, and mismatched state/answer generations. No unsupported property may disappear through conversion.

## Safe conversion

Answers replace only the contract identity and normalize the documented effective defaults: single domain mode, enabled triage, the five default labels, and an empty domains list. Domain IDs represent an unordered collection and use canonical sorted order. Validate distinct safe labels and domain requirements before conversion. Preserve every supplied decision.

State replaces its contract identity and converts its nested historical answers by the same rule. Preserve version, Copier version, template hash, every managed path/root/hash/kind, managed-file ordering, and directory ordering. The pure conversion does not render templates or update hashes. Its preservation value is the complete validated state with contract identities normalized and effective answer defaults applied. It never omits an accepted field. Destination validation and shared deep equality must pass before persistence.

## Owning transaction

Setup can modify multiple managed files, so it does not call shared single-file persistence on the live state before applying its plan. Instead, it copies historical input to an owned temporary artifact and calls shared `safeUpgrade` with this installed adapter and operation `upgrade`. The shared engine resolves this declared procedure, validates preservation, and commits only the temporary artifact. Setup reads that validated current content and removes the temporary directory.

Read-only plan/check never change source bytes. Approved init alone may persist regenerated state and managed-file changes through the existing setup transaction, after conflict detection and freshness checks. Any deliberate regenerated values appear in the exact approval plan; they are not part of contract conversion. Neither historical interpretation nor conversion grants setup approval.

## Boundaries

The adapter supports pure `upgrade` only. Mutation requests fail. It refuses event, snapshot, and review paths. Unknown or unsafe input fails without live writes. External shared-context route/layout formats, hosted tracker API formats, and Copier configuration remain under their existing owners.


The declared shared single-file upgrade rejects non-JSON YAML containing `#` before persistence. The JSON converter cannot retain authored YAML comments. This conservative guard also rejects `#` inside YAML strings. Rejection preserves the original bytes; use a comment-preserving editor for those files. Valid JSON strings containing `#` remain supported. Normal setup reads the answers without rewriting their source; plan/check stay read-only, and authorized init can still use commented historical answers.
